7. <u>Solid-Waste Disposal</u>. Non-combustible solid wastes such as batteries and all plastics and rubber products will be back-loaded to McMurdo Station for removal to a disposal point outside the Treaty area. The disposal point will be the U.S. Navy's salvage yard at Port Hueneme, California. Non-combustible solid wastes other than that specified above will be buried in a snow pit and covered before the camp is evacuated, it will be suitably marked. This disposal method indirectly follows the criterion of SCAR Circular 292 which recommends an oceanic fate for material of this type, where possible. The ultimate oceanic fate will follow a long period of in-transit storage, estimated to be perhaps 1,000 years at the present calculated rate of ice movement.
8. <u>Liquid-Waste Disposal</u>. Sanitary wastes will be managed by subsurface discharge to the firm. This is a proven and accepted technique which has been employed in both the Arctic and Antarctic (Reed, 1965; Reed and Tobiasson 1966, 1968).
The wastewaters percolate downward through the permeable firn. Depth of vertical penetration is dependent on the <u>in-situ</u> temperature, and the volumne and temperature of the wastewater. In no case will there be sufficient residual heat to cause significant melting in the underlying impermeable ice. There is, therefore, no possibility of direct contact of these wastewaters with the seawater underlying the shelf.
